user_saw: Changing Visitor Access maxVisitors or defaultTtlDays while agent turns were running queued a full plugin replacement, so the config update timed out, readiness failed and new runs were delayed.
summary: Declared visitor limit settings as hot-reload prefixes read live from committed runtime config, and let the loader lend the retained Gateway plugin instance only when the run's plugin config matches committed config.
reasoning: Visitor Access (older than the graft) always captured its config at registration, so any config edit required plugin replacement; that was fine until the reload machinery evolved to gate new agent work behind exclusive replacement that drains held turns (e.g. 88fff4ed5ae, 2d5c68187a3, 62e0b2b7fcf), turning a limit edit into a 60 s blocked window. No single commit broke a previously working path that I can quote, and the drain gating is deliberate design, so this is a long-standing plugin contract exposed by changes outside it rather than a regression; I could not pin one trigger commit.
